rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: Finite sets and maps: a map between finite sets of equal cardinality is injective exactly when it is bijective; a set of cardinality at most $|U|$ injects into $U$; unique factorisation in $\Z$ (the Gödel code).

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: Sufficiency: minimal sufficient statistics are unique up to bijection; invoked as motivation only --- no probability enters, the operative notion is set-theoretic (B3).

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: The corpus: the shell $\Fp$, $\p=4\chron+1$, with its frame and quarter-turn (1:B2, B3); its frames $x\mapsto a+bx$ (1:C2; 00:C1); the Carrier and its readings as incomplete projections (00:A8, A6); finiteness and counting by return (00:A4, A7); $4\mid\p-1$ from the two involutions (00:B3); consolidation as frame maps, innovation as the extension $\Fpq$ where $\sqrt\nu$ is written (3:B5).

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: The empirical record: cross-modal alignment and unsupervised translation between independently trained embeddings; grokking; emergence, transfer under shared structure, latent knowledge, interpolation of arbitrary labels; hyperspherical embeddings; floating point as a finite subset of $\R$; sphere packing.

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: The latent domain: a finite set $\mathcal Z\subset\mathcal U_t=\Fp$, the complete relational domain a model reconstructs from its data; the shell is the ambient set and a reading of it is a projection (00:A6).

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: Observation maps: $g_m:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X_m$ deterministic, one per modality, carrying its resolution; no stochastic model and no conditional independence is assumed; every cross-modal relation factors through $\mathcal Z$.

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: Adequacy: $E_m:\mathcal X_m\to W_m$ is adequate when $E_m\circ g_m=\varphi_m$ is a bijection $\mathcal Z\to W_m$; minimality, $W_m=\varphi_m(\mathcal Z)$, is part of the bijection, so the minimal adequate representation of Section~\ref{sec:background} and Definition~\ref{def:adequate} are one notion.

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: Adequacy makes the observation map injective on the latent domain: $g_m(z)=g_m(z')$ forces $z=z'$; $\mathcal Z$ is the domain modality $m$ resolves completely.

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: Uniqueness up to bijection: for adequate $E_1$, $E_2$ of one $g$, $\psi=\varphi_2\circ\varphi_1^{-1}:W_1\to W_2$ is a bijection with $E_2\circ g=\psi\circ E_1\circ g$ --- $E_2=\psi\circ E_1$ on $g(\mathcal Z)$, on all of $\mathcal X$ when $\mathcal X=g(\mathcal Z)$; $\psi$ is the unique map with this property.
rows.source: Lemma~\ref{lem:uniq_min_adequate}; Lemma~\ref{lem:minimalUniqueBackground}; \src{A2}, \src{A3}; \lean{Representation.transition\_exists, Representation.transition\_unique, FRC.Representation.transition\_spec, FRC.Representation.transitionBij, FRC.Representation.transition\_unique}

rows.label: B6
rows.predicate: The embedding into the shell: $|W_m|=|\mathcal Z|\le\p$, so an injection $\iota_m:W_m\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_t$ exists --- the one place finiteness enters; canonically $\iota_m=\varphi_m^{-1}$ followed by the inclusion; $\psi_m:=\iota_m\circ\varphi_m:\mathcal Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_t$ is modality $m$'s chart of $\mathcal Z$.

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: Theorem~\ref{thm:UST} (i), (ii): every chart $\psi_m$ is injective, and $\Psi_{m\to n}:=\psi_n\circ\psi_m^{-1}:\psi_m(\mathcal Z)\to\psi_n(\mathcal Z)$ is a well-defined bijection, with $\Psi_{n\to k}\circ\Psi_{m\to n}=\Psi_{m\to k}$ and $\Psi_{m\to m}$ the identity.

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: Theorem~\ref{thm:UST} (iii): with $\iota_m=\varphi_m^{-1}$ every chart is the inclusion $\mathcal Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_t$ and $\psi(\mathcal Z)=\mathcal Z$; canonical structurally (unique once $\mathcal Z$ is fixed), not algorithmically; ``subspace'' means subset.

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: The canonical lift $L_m:=\varphi_m^{-1}\circ E_m:\mathcal X_m\to\mathcal Z$ satisfies $L_m\circ g_m=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal Z}$, and $L_m(x)$ is the unique $z$ with $E_m(x)=\varphi_m(z)$.

rows.label: C4
rows.predicate: Cross-modal consistency: $\psi\circ L_m\circ g_m=\psi\circ L_n\circ g_n=\psi$ --- observations of one latent state lift to one point --- and $\iota_m(W_m)=\iota_n(W_n)=\psi(\mathcal Z)=\mathcal Z$.

rows.label: C5
rows.predicate: Charts of the shell itself: for $\mathcal Z=\Fp$ the charts respecting the arithmetic are the frames $x\mapsto a+bx$ (1:C2), $\p(\p-1)$ of them, and $\Psi_{m\to n}$ between two frames is the one affine map carrying the first to the second (simply transitive) --- the corpus's coordinate systems are the paper's charts.

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: Foundational embeddings are adequate representations of one finite latent domain: cross-modal alignment, transferability and semantic coherence are the bijections $\Psi_{m\to n}$ (C1), consequences of the shared domain, not of architecture; the empirical record (A4) is their registered consequence. Falsifier: two adequate embeddings of one domain with no bijective translation on the resolved states.

rows.label: D2
rows.predicate: Scope and limits: the theorem uses the finiteness of $\mathcal Z$ alone, no algebraic or geometric property of $\mathcal U_t$; the shell as host is the ontology's claim (A3); optimisation decides when a representation is recovered, not which; non-stationary or weakly factorisable data may admit none; coordinate alignment may be intractable; nonlinearity as expansion and depth as shell complexity are analogies (Y1).

rows.label: E1
rows.predicate: The hypersphere [chart]: a Euclidean chart $\mathrm{Emb}:\mathcal Z\to\R^{d}$ equivariant for a symmetry acting transitively on $\mathcal Z$ and orthogonally on $\R^{d}$ has constant norm --- $\mathrm{Emb}(\mathcal Z)\subset S^{d-1}$. The shell's character chart $z\mapsto(\cos2\pi kz/\p,\sin2\pi kz/\p)_{k}$ is such a chart under translation, $\|\mathrm{Emb}(z)\|^{2}=\p-1$; in the shell's arithmetic $\sum_{k}\g^{kz}\g^{k(n-z)}=n$ for every $z$.

rows.label: E2
rows.predicate: Quantisation [chart]: a digital embedding has coordinates in a finite $\mathcal Q\subset\R$; at step $\Delta$ the distinguishable points on a sphere of radius $R$ number $N(R)\sim C_d(R/\Delta)^{d-1}$ (grid counts fit exponent $d-1$ at $d=2,3$); at fixed $d$, $\Delta$ the capacity grows with $R$.

rows.label: E3
rows.predicate: Gödel collapse: for distinct primes $p_1,\dots,p_d$ the code $G(x)=\prod p_i^{x_i}$ is injective on $\N^{d}$ (unique factorisation), and $G\bmod q$ stays injective on a finite set once $q$ exceeds its maximum; instance $d=3$, $x_i\le4$, primes $2,3,5$: $125$ codes, maximum $810\,000$, $q=810\,013$; signed coordinates are shifted first.

rows.label: E4
rows.predicate: The reading of Section~\ref{sec:hypersphere}: the sphere is the continuous shadow of the shell --- uniform radius the absence of intrinsic attributes, direction the relational content; the coordinate count is a representational artefact, every quantised vector one element of one field (E3); the radius reads the resolved domain's size; Gödel codes establish representability only, not geometry or training.

rows.label: V1
rows.predicate: The package \texttt{src/4-representation} (\texttt{finite-ring-space}; $13$ checks, $11$ exact and $2$ chart, standard library only): \src{a\_adequacy} A1--A5 (every finite model with $|\mathcal Z|\le3$, $|\mathcal X|\le4$: adequacy, the transition and its uniqueness, Theorem~\ref{thm:UST}, the lifts), \src{b\_shell} B1--B3 (the host shell, the frames as charts, the $\F_{13}$ instance), \src{c\_geometry} C1--C5 (the character chart, the quantisation count, the Gödel code).

rows.label: V2
rows.predicate: \texttt{lean/FrcLedger/Representation.lean} (Mathlib; classical, tier~2): fourteen declarations --- B3--B6, C1--C4 for arbitrary types, E1 for a transitive isometric action, E3 by unique factorisation. \texttt{lean/FrcCore/Representation.lean} (no Mathlib, \emph{no axioms}, tier~0): B3--B6, C1--C4 pointwise, with bijections as data; E3 on two primes; E1 in the shell's arithmetic; C5 by the frame group (1:C2).

rows.label: Y1
rows.predicate: Depth and the shell hierarchy: whether nonlinear layers correspond to innovation steps $\mathcal U_t\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_{t+1}$ and depth to arithmetic complexity (Interpretations~\ref{interp:nonlinear}, \ref{interp:complexity}) as a theorem; named as future work (iii), not claimed.

rows.label: T1
rows.predicate: Learning objectives as approximations of adequacy (contrastive, masked prediction), algorithms for the projection maps $g_m$, and a general algebraic account of multimodal learning; named as future work (i), (ii), (iv), not claimed.

legend.name: Import
legend.text: A standard result, or a corpus result, used without reproof.

legend.name: Definition
legend.text: A naming or declared convention, carrying no empirical content.

legend.name: Theorem
legend.text: Derived, and machine-verified in exact arithmetic by the named witness.

legend.name: Realisation

B4.name: FRC.Representation.adequate_inj
B4.doc: 4:B4: adequacy makes the observation map injective on the latent domain.

B4.name: FRC.Representation.adequate_inj
B4.doc: 4:B4 — adequacy makes the observation map injective on the latent domain: `g z₁ = g z₂ → z₁ = z₂`.

B5.name: FRC.Representation.transition_exists
B5.doc: 4:B5 (Lemma 2): two adequate representations of one observation map are related by the bijection `ψ = φ₂ ∘ φ₁⁻¹ : W₁ ≃ W₂` on the resolved observations, `E₂ ∘ g = ψ ∘ E₁ ∘ g`.

B5.name: FRC.Representation.transition_unique
B5.doc: 4:B5 (the uniqueness clause): a map with that property is determined by it, since `E₁ ∘ g` is onto `W₁`.

B5.name: FRC.Representation.transitionBij
B5.doc: 4:B5 — the transition is a bijection `W₁ → W₂`: its inverse is `φ₁ ∘ φ₂⁻¹`.

B5.name: FRC.Representation.transition_unique
B5.doc: 4:B5 (the uniqueness clause) — any `ψ'` with `E₂ (g z) = ψ' (E₁ (g z))` for every `z` agrees with the transition on all of `W₁`, because `E₁ ∘ g` is onto `W₁`.

B6.name: FRC.Representation.embeds_in_shell
B6.doc: 4:B6: a representation space of the cardinality of the latent domain embeds injectively in the shell — the one place where finiteness enters.

B6.name: FRC.Representation.canonical_iota
B6.doc: 4:B6, 4:C2 (Theorem 1 (iii), the canonical choice): with `incl : Z → U` the inclusion of the latent domain and `φ = E ∘ g`, the embedding `ι := incl ∘ φ⁻¹` is injective and `ι ∘ φ = incl` — the chart `ψ_m` is the inclusion.

B6.name: FRC.Representation.iota_inj
B6.doc: 4:B6 — `ι` is injective when the inclusion is.

C1.name: FRC.Representation.chart_injective
C1.doc: 4:C1 (Theorem 1 (i)): the chart `ψ_m = ι_m ∘ φ_m` is injective for every injective `ι_m`.

C1.name: FRC.Representation.transition_images
C1.doc: 4:C1 (Theorem 1 (ii)): the transition `Ψ_{m→n} = ψ_n ∘ ψ_m⁻¹` is a bijection between the images, carrying `ψ_m z` to `ψ_n z`.

C1.name: FRC.Representation.chart_inj
C1.doc: 4:C1 (Theorem 1 (i)) — the chart `ψ = ι ∘ E ∘ g` is injective for any injective `ι`.

C1.name: FRC.Representation.transition_graph
C1.doc: 4:C1 (Theorem 1 (ii)) — the transition `Ψ_{m→n} = ψ_n ∘ ψ_m⁻¹` is well defined and bijective between the images: two latent states have the same `ψ_m`-image exactly when they have the same `ψ_n`-image, so the pairs `(ψ_m z, ψ_n z)` are the graph of a bijection `ψ_m(Z) → ψ_n(Z)`.

C2.name: FRC.Representation.canonical_iota
C2.doc: 4:B6, 4:C2 (Theorem 1 (iii), the canonical choice): with `incl : Z → U` the inclusion of the latent domain and `φ = E ∘ g`, the embedding `ι := incl ∘ φ⁻¹` is injective and `ι ∘ φ = incl` — the chart `ψ_m` is the inclusion.

C2.name: FRC.Representation.canonical_chart
C2.doc: 4:C2 (Theorem 1 (iii)) — in the canonical parametrisation every chart is the inclusion: `ι (E (g z)) = incl z`.

C3.name: FRC.Representation.lift
C3.doc: 4:C3 (Corollary 1): the lift `L = φ⁻¹ ∘ E : X → Z` recovers the latent state, `L ∘ g = id`, and `L x` is the unique `z` with `E x = φ z`.

C3.name: FRC.Representation.lift_g
C3.doc: 4:C3 — the lift recovers the latent state, `L (g z) = z`.

C3.name: FRC.Representation.lift_unique
C3.doc: 4:C3 — `L x` is the unique `z` with `E x = φ z`.

C4.name: FRC.Representation.consistency
C4.doc: 4:C4 (Corollary 2): the lifts of two modalities' observations of one latent state agree, so the canonical charts `ψ ∘ L_m ∘ g_m` and `ψ ∘ L_n ∘ g_n` both equal `ψ`.

C4.name: FRC.Representation.consistency
C4.doc: 4:C4 (Corollary 2) — cross-modal consistency: the lifts of two modalities' observations of one latent state agree, `L_m (g_m z) = L_n (g_n z)`, hence so do their canonical charts `ψ ∘ L_m ∘ g_m = ψ = ψ ∘ L_n ∘ g_n`.

C5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.Affine.simply_transitive
C5.doc: 1:C2, 4:C5 (the frame group), simple transitivity — for frames `(a, b)` and `(c, d)` (`b, d ≠ 0`) there is exactly one affine map carrying the first to the second: `φ (a, b) := (φ.apply a, φ.b · b)`.

C5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frame_count
C5.doc: 1:C2, 4:C5, the order — the frames `(a, b)`, `b ≠ 0`, number `p·(p − 1)`: `p` choices of the origin, `p − 1` of the unit.

E1.name: FRC.Representation.sphere_of_equivariant
E1.doc: 4:E1 (the hypersphere): a Euclidean chart `emb : Z → E` equivariant for a symmetry that acts transitively on the domain and by linear isometries on the space has constant norm — its image lies on one sphere about the origin.

E1.name: FRC.Representation.Shell.charChart_shift
E1.doc: 4:E1 (equivariance) — translation by `a` multiplies coordinate `k` by `g^{ka}`: the shell's translations act on the chart coordinatewise, as the rotations act on the Fourier embedding.

E1.name: FRC.Representation.Shell.charChart_norm
E1.doc: 4:E1 (constant norm) — the conjugate norm `Σ_{k<n} g^{kz} g^{k(n−z)}` of the chart equals `n = p − 1` for every `z ≤ n`: every point of the chart lies on one sphere, exactly.

E3.name: FRC.Representation.godel_injective
E3.doc: 4:E3 (Gödel encoding): over distinct primes `p₁, …, p_d` the code `x ↦ ∏ pᵢ^{xᵢ}` is injective on `ℕ^d` — unique factorisation.

E3.name: FRC.Representation.mod_injective
E3.doc: 4:E3 (the reduction into one field): an injective integer code with values below `q` stays injective modulo `q`.

E3.name: FRC.Representation.godel_instance
E3.doc: 4:E3 (the instance of the package): with `d = 3`, exponents `≤ 4` and the primes `2, 3, 5`, the code is at most `2⁴3⁴5⁴ = 810 000`, and `q = 810 013` is the least prime above it.

E3.name: FRC.Representation.godel2_inj
E3.doc: 4:E3 (Gödel encoding, two primes) — `2^a 3^b = 2^c 3^d` forces `a = c` and `b = d`: the code is injective, by parity and cancellation; the general case over `d` distinct primes is `FrcLedger.Representation.godel_injective`.

E3.name: FRC.Representation.mod_injective
E3.doc: 4:E3 (the reduction into the shell) — an injective integer code with values below `q` stays injective modulo `q`: `f a % q = f b % q` forces `f a = f b`.
